questions.question: Choose the correct option: By the time we reached the station, the train ___.
questions.explanation: The past perfect marks an action completed before another past action.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: She ___ in this school since 2022.
questions.explanation: The present perfect continuous describes an activity that began in the past and continues now.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: When I called, they ___ dinner.
questions.explanation: The past continuous describes an action in progress at a particular past time.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: This time next week, we ___ our examinations.
questions.explanation: The future continuous describes an activity that will be in progress at a future time.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: The parcel ___ before noon yesterday.
questions.explanation: The passive voice is appropriate because the parcel receives the action.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: The manager asked whether I ___ the report.
questions.explanation: In reported speech with a past reporting verb, the present perfect commonly backshifts to past perfect.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: He said, “I am busy.” Choose the correct reported form.
options: He said that he is busy.
He said that he was busy.
He says that he had busy.
He said that I was busy.
questions.explanation: The present 'am' backshifts to 'was' in standard reported speech.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: The teacher said, “Do not make noise.”
options: The teacher told us do not make noise.
The teacher told us not to make noise.
The teacher said us not making noise.
The teacher asked that not make noise.
questions.explanation: Negative commands are commonly reported with 'told/asked + object + not to + verb'.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: She asked me, “Where do you live?”
options: She asked me where did I live.
She asked me where I lived.
She asked me where do I live.
She asked where I live did.
questions.explanation: Reported questions use statement word order, without do-support inversion.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: He asked, “Have you seen my keys?”
options: He asked whether I had seen his keys.
He asked have I seen his keys.
He asked whether had I seen my keys.
He asked that I saw his keys.
questions.explanation: Yes/no questions can be reported with 'whether' and normal statement word order.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: You ___ wear a helmet while riding a motorcycle; it is required by law.
questions.explanation: 'Must' expresses a strong obligation.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: You ___ have told me earlier; I could have helped.
questions.explanation: 'Should have' expresses a past action that was advisable but did not occur.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: The lights are off; they ___ have gone to bed.
questions.explanation: 'Must have' expresses a strong deduction about a past situation.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: You ___ bring food; refreshments will be provided.
questions.explanation: 'Needn't' expresses absence of necessity.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: ___ you mind opening the window?
questions.explanation: 'Would you mind...?' is a polite request pattern.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: There is ___ sugar left, so we can make tea.
questions.explanation: 'Sugar' is uncountable; 'a little' means a small amount that is available.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: Only ___ students submitted the optional task.
questions.explanation: 'Students' is countable plural, so 'a few' is appropriate.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: I have ___ information about the event than you do.
questions.explanation: 'Information' is uncountable and takes 'less' in standard usage.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: There are ___ mistakes in this draft than in the first one.
questions.explanation: 'Mistakes' is countable plural, so 'fewer' is appropriate.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: Neither of the two explanations ___ convincing.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is conventionally singular in formal agreement.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: The quality of these products ___ improved.
questions.explanation: The head noun 'quality' is singular, so it takes 'has'.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: The captain, along with the players, ___ arriving shortly.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'along with the players' does not change the singular subject 'captain'.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: Each of the answers ___ a reason.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular and takes 'has'.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: The scissors ___ on the table.
questions.explanation: 'Scissors' is a plural-form noun and normally takes a plural verb.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: A pair of scissors ___ missing.
questions.explanation: The subject is the singular phrase 'a pair'.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: The teacher as well as the students ___ present.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'teacher' controls agreement in 'as well as' constructions.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: Choose the correct article: She is ___ honest officer.
questions.explanation: 'Honest' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an' is used.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: He is ___ university student.
questions.explanation: 'University' begins with a /juː/ consonant sound, so 'a' is used.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: We usually have ___ breakfast at seven.
questions.explanation: Meals used in a general sense commonly take no article.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: ___ Himalayas are a major mountain range.
questions.explanation: Names of mountain ranges generally take 'the'.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: She plays ___ violin in the school orchestra.
questions.explanation: Musical instruments commonly take 'the' with 'play'.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: The children were divided ___ four groups.
questions.explanation: 'Divide into' introduces the resulting groups.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: The teacher congratulated Ravi ___ his success.
questions.explanation: The standard collocation is 'congratulate someone on something'.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: She is capable ___ solving the puzzle.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'capable' is followed by 'of'.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: We have been waiting ___ the bus for twenty minutes.
questions.explanation: 'Wait for' is the usual verb-preposition combination for expecting transport.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: He apologized ___ being late.
questions.explanation: 'Apologize for' introduces the action or reason.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: The result depends ___ how carefully you work.
questions.explanation: 'Depend on' is the standard collocation.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: She insisted ___ paying for the meal.
questions.explanation: 'Insist on' is followed by a noun or gerund.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: The book was translated ___ Telugu.
questions.explanation: 'Translate into' identifies the language of the resulting text.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: He is familiar ___ the new software.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'familiar' is followed by 'with' when someone knows something.

questions.question: Choose the correct phrasal verb: Please ___ the form before submitting it.
questions.explanation: 'Fill in' means complete a form by adding information.

questions.question: Choose the correct phrasal verb: The meeting was ___ because the speaker was ill.
questions.explanation: 'Put off' means postpone.

questions.question: Choose the correct phrasal verb: Could you ___ this word in a dictionary?
questions.explanation: 'Look up' means search for information in a reference source.

questions.question: Choose the correct phrasal verb: The nurse will ___ the patient while the doctor is away.
questions.explanation: 'Look after' means take care of.

questions.question: Choose the correct phrasal verb: The old building was ___ to make room for a library.
questions.explanation: 'Pull down' can mean demolish a building.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: The new policy will ___ all employees.
questions.explanation: 'Affect' is the verb meaning influence.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: The medicine had an immediate ___.
questions.explanation: 'Effect' is a noun meaning a result or consequence.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: The school will ___ a survey next month.
questions.explanation: 'Conduct a survey' is the appropriate collocation.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: Please ___ your answer with evidence from the passage.
questions.explanation: 'Justify' is the verb meaning provide reasons or evidence for a claim.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: The instructions were ___, so nobody misunderstood them.
questions.explanation: 'Explicit' means stated clearly and directly.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: The meaning was ___ rather than directly stated.
questions.explanation: 'Implicit' means suggested or understood without being directly stated.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: A person who can use two languages is ___.
questions.explanation: 'Bilingual' means able to use two languages.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: A word with the opposite meaning is an ___.
questions.explanation: An antonym is a word opposite in meaning to another word.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: Words that sound alike but differ in meaning and often spelling are ___.
questions.explanation: Homophones share pronunciation but have different meanings and often different spellings.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: A word formed from the initial letters of a phrase and pronounced as a word is a(n) ___.
questions.explanation: An acronym is formed from initial letters and pronounced as a word, such as 'UNESCO'.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of 'meticulous'.
questions.explanation: 'Meticulous' means showing great attention to detail.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of 'diligent'.
questions.explanation: 'Diligent' means careful and persistent in one's work.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of 'obsolete'.
questions.explanation: 'Obsolete' means no longer in use or no longer useful.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of 'relieve'.
questions.explanation: 'Relieve' means reduce pain, difficulty or distress.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of 'coherent'.
questions.explanation: 'Coherent' describes ideas that are logically connected and understandable.

questions.question: Choose the antonym of 'hostile'.
questions.explanation: 'Friendly' contrasts with hostile.

questions.question: Choose the antonym of 'temporary'.
questions.explanation: 'Permanent' means lasting or intended to last indefinitely.

questions.question: Choose the antonym of 'optimistic'.
questions.explanation: 'Pessimistic' contrasts with optimistic.

questions.question: Choose the antonym of 'transparent'.
questions.explanation: 'Opaque' means not allowing light through; it contrasts with transparent.

questions.question: Choose the antonym of 'frequent'.
questions.explanation: 'Infrequent' means happening rarely, the opposite of frequent.

questions.question: What does the idiom 'spill the beans' mean?
questions.explanation: The idiom means disclose secret information.

questions.question: What does 'get cold feet' mean?
questions.explanation: The idiom describes becoming nervous and reluctant to proceed.

questions.question: What does 'a blessing in disguise' mean?
options: Something that seems bad at first but leads to a good result
A gift hidden in a room
questions.explanation: The phrase describes an apparent misfortune that turns out beneficial.

questions.question: What does 'keep an eye on' mean?
questions.explanation: The idiom means watch something or someone carefully.

questions.question: What does 'cost an arm and a leg' mean?
questions.explanation: The idiom means cost a great deal of money.

questions.question: Which sentence is in the subjunctive mood?
options: I suggest that he be present at the meeting.
He is present at the meeting.
questions.explanation: The mandative subjunctive uses the base form 'be' after expressions such as 'suggest that'.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a relative pronoun correctly?
options: The woman whom I met was helpful.
The woman which I met was helpful.
The woman whose I met was helpful.
The woman where I met was helpful.
questions.explanation: 'Whom' can function as the object of 'met' when referring to a person.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'who' as a subject pronoun?
options: The student who answered first received a certificate.
The student whom answered first received a certificate.
The student which answered first received a certificate.
The student whose answered first received a certificate.
questions.explanation: 'Who' is the subject of the relative clause 'who answered first'.

questions.question: Which sentence contains a participial phrase?
options: Feeling exhausted, Maya went to bed early.
Maya went to bed early because she was exhausted.
Maya was exhausted and went to bed.
questions.explanation: 'Feeling exhausted' is a participial phrase modifying Maya.

questions.question: Which sentence contains an infinitive of purpose?
options: He went to the library to borrow a book.
questions.explanation: 'To borrow a book' explains the purpose of going to the library.

questions.question: Which sentence is grammatically parallel?
options: The course teaches learners to read, to write and to speak clearly.
The course teaches learners reading, to write and speaking clearly.
The course teaches learners to read, writing and to speak clearly.
The course teaches learners read, to writing and speak clearly.
questions.explanation: The three infinitive phrases have matching grammatical form.

questions.question: Which option best combines the sentences: 'The road was flooded. We took another route.'
options: The road was flooded, so we took another route.
The road was flooded because we took another route.
Although the road was flooded, so we took another route.
The road flooded, unless we took another route.
questions.explanation: 'So' correctly signals the result of the flooded road.

questions.question: Which option best combines: 'She practised daily. She improved her pronunciation.'
options: She improved her pronunciation because she practised daily.
She practised daily unless she improved her pronunciation.
She improved her pronunciation, but she practised daily.
She practised daily although she improved her pronunciation.
questions.explanation: 'Because' connects the improvement with its reason.

questions.question: Which sentence is an appropriate formal email closing?
questions.explanation: 'Yours sincerely' is a conventional formal closing when the recipient is named.

questions.question: Which sentence is most suitable for a formal report?
options: The findings indicate a gradual increase in attendance.
Attendance went up loads, which was pretty cool.
Kids came in more, I guess.
Lots more people showed up, sort of.
questions.explanation: The first sentence uses precise, objective language suited to a report.

questions.question: Which sentence best avoids wordiness?
options: The meeting was postponed to a later future date.
The meeting was postponed and delayed until later on.
The meeting was postponed at a point in time later.
questions.explanation: The concise sentence communicates the information without redundant wording.

questions.question: Which is the best paraphrase of 'The task was challenging, but achievable'?
options: The task was difficult yet possible to complete.
The task was impossible to finish.
The task was simple and required no effort.
The task was difficult, so it was abandoned.
questions.explanation: The paraphrase preserves both ideas: difficulty and possibility.

questions.question: Which note-taking method organizes ideas around a central topic with branches?
questions.explanation: A mind map places a central idea at the centre and connects related ideas through branches.

questions.question: Which strategy is most useful when a learner encounters an unfamiliar word while reading?
options: Use context clues and word parts before checking a dictionary
Assume the first guessed meaning is always correct
Stop reading and memorize the entire page
questions.explanation: Context and morphology can help infer meaning; a dictionary can then confirm it.

questions.question: Which task primarily assesses inferential reading?
options: Explain why a character may have acted as they did using clues from the story
Copy a sentence stated in the passage
Count the words in the title
questions.explanation: Inference requires interpreting clues beyond directly stated information.

questions.question: Which task primarily assesses critical reading?
options: Examine whether the writer's evidence supports the claim
Match a word to its dictionary definition
Read the passage aloud at a steady pace
questions.explanation: Critical reading evaluates claims, reasoning and supporting evidence.

questions.question: Which activity can help learners recognize a text's organization?
options: Label the introduction, supporting points and conclusion
Count the letters in each sentence
Copy every noun into a list
questions.explanation: Identifying text sections helps learners notice structure and organization.

questions.question: Which is a suitable while-listening activity for a short dialogue?
options: Complete a table with key details such as place, time and purpose
Predict the title after the recording ends
Copy the transcript before the audio begins
questions.explanation: A focused information table directs attention to key details during listening.

questions.question: Which is a useful post-listening activity?
options: Compare answers and discuss which clues in the audio support them
Guess the topic without hearing the audio
Repeat the audio's first word only
questions.explanation: Reviewing answers against audio evidence consolidates comprehension.

questions.question: Which teacher prompt is most likely to elicit an extended spoken response?
options: What led you to that conclusion? Explain your reasoning.
questions.explanation: An open prompt asking for reasoning encourages a longer, elaborated response.

questions.question: Which activity gives learners a reason to exchange information orally?
options: An information-gap task where each partner has different details
Individual word matching with all answers shown
Teacher lecture with no learner response
questions.explanation: An information gap creates a communicative need to ask and share information.

questions.question: Which feature is essential to a useful writing rubric?
options: Clear criteria that describe observable qualities of the work
A score based only on handwriting
Different criteria for each learner without explanation
questions.explanation: Clear, observable criteria make expectations and feedback understandable.

questions.question: Which feedback comment is most actionable?
options: Add a topic sentence that states the paragraph's main idea.
Your writing is not good enough.
questions.explanation: The comment identifies a specific revision the learner can make.

questions.question: Which assessment is formative?
options: A brief exit ticket used to plan the next lesson
A final examination used only to certify completion
A certificate awarded at the end of the year
A rank published after the course
questions.explanation: Formative assessment gathers evidence during learning to guide next steps.

questions.question: Which assessment is summative?
options: An end-of-unit test used to report achievement
A mid-lesson question used to adjust explanation
A quick thumbs-up check before practice
questions.explanation: Summative assessment evaluates achievement at the end of a learning period.

questions.question: Which practice improves the fairness of a language test?
options: Ensure tasks align with taught objectives and provide accessible, clear instructions
Include obscure content unrelated to the construct
Use confusing wording to increase difficulty
Change scoring criteria after seeing responses
questions.explanation: Alignment and clear access reduce irrelevant barriers to demonstrating the target skill.

questions.question: Which statement describes reliability in assessment?
options: The results are reasonably consistent across comparable occasions or raters
The test measures exactly the intended construct
The test is enjoyable for every learner
The test contains a large number of pages
questions.explanation: Reliability concerns consistency of measurement.

questions.question: Which statement describes validity in assessment?
options: The assessment supports the intended interpretation of what learners know or can do
The same score is always produced by every test
questions.explanation: Validity concerns whether evidence supports the intended interpretation and use of results.

questions.question: Which is an example of self-assessment?
options: A learner uses success criteria to review their own draft and set a goal
A parent signs a permission slip
A peer assigns a grade without criteria
questions.explanation: Self-assessment involves learners judging their own work against criteria and identifying next steps.

questions.question: Which approach best supports mixed-proficiency groups?
options: Use flexible grouping and scaffold tasks while keeping meaningful shared goals
Permanently separate learners by presumed ability
Give advanced learners all teaching responsibilities
Remove challenging content from every task
questions.explanation: Flexible grouping and scaffolding respond to needs without fixed labels or eliminating worthwhile learning.
